subtitle: An announcement of a two-day training course in NLS for network site coordinators.

tldr.problem: Network sites needed staff trained to help others use the Network Information Center and NLS system.

today: RFC 276 documents training efforts for the very early ARPA network in autumn 1971, showing how the Network Information Center invested in building user competency across the distributed network community.

sections.title: The Training Opportunity
sections.content:
The Network Information Center at SRI-ARC announced a two-day course to be held on November 29 and 30, 1971. The course taught participants how to use NLS, the Network Information Center's online system, and how to use the Journal function within it.

Richard Watson of SRI-ARC organized the course to help people become local experts who could support their colleagues at other network sites in accessing and using the NIC's resources.
sections.eli5: The NIC offered a class to teach people how to use its online computer system.

sections.title: Target Participants
sections.content:
The course was specifically designed for station agents and secretaries at network sites. These were the people who could become local support resources for their organizations. They could help colleagues get started with NLS and could transcribe documents and messages into the online system.

Though primarily aimed at this administrative audience, the course was open to anyone interested, subject only to a limit of 12 participants.
sections.eli5: The class was for people who help others, like secretaries and coordinators at different network sites.

sections.title: Course Logistics
sections.content:
The course was held at SRI-ARC in California. Interested participants could contact Dirk Van Nouhuys or Dick Watson at SRI-ARC by telephone at (415) 326-6200, extensions 3370 or 2013 to register.

For attendees traveling from other sites, the NIC offered to make motel reservations, typically at the Mermaid Motel in nearby Menlo Park. This logistics support reflected the importance the NIC placed on distributing knowledge of its system throughout the network community.
sections.eli5: The class was in California, and the organizers would help people find a place to stay.
